title: add interleaved-shot consistency validator and fuzzy-threshold ci hook
author: Anjali Rao
description: Motivation: Some prompt-sets show non-deterministic score variance across interleaved few-shot orderings and sampling seeds which can cause flaky CI failures or missed regressions. This PR introduces an interleaved-shot consistency validator plus a fuzzy-threshold CI hook that smooths tiny, non-actionable deltas while still surfacing meaningful regressions. Design summary: 1) interleaved-shot validator runs configurable permutations of k-shot examples (interleaved ordering) and computes a pairwise consistency score distribution for each prompt in a set; 2) fuzzy-threshold hook aggregates prompt-level distributions into cohort-level statistics and applies a tunable soft-threshold with an exponential smoothing window so transient noise does not fail CI; 3) exposes knobs for sample count, permutation strategy, alpha for smoothing, and minimum effect size. Implementation details: added a new validator module eval_harness/validators/interleaved_shot.py that implements permutation sampling and consistency metrics, added a compact consistency metric to eval_harness/metrics/consistency_metric.py, and added a CI adapter ci/hooks/fuzzy_threshold_adapter.py that integrates with existing eval-orchestration state machine. Tests and docs: unit tests and a smoke suite were added under eval_harness/tests, and docs/quality_gates.md updated with usage examples and rollout guidance. Rollout plan: default hook disabled; enable as an opt-in gate for canary branches and then roll to baseline projects after two weeks of stability. Why this is different: instead of hard binary thresholds this approach models intra-prompt ordering variance explicitly and uses a probabilistic smoothing gate to reduce noisy CI churn while preserving signal fidelity. Backward compatibility: config defaults are conservative to avoid changing existing gate behavior. Checklist: [x] validator implemented, [x] CI adapter wired into pipeline, [x] unit + smoke tests, [x] docs updated, [x] Linear ticket linked. Related work: inspired by ENG-6121 prompt-order robustness work but focuses on CI gating behavior rather than offline eval metrics.
